outputs.exact_statement: Let $$k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2),$$ where $q,H_1,H_2$ are algebraically independent. There exist a finite-dimensional associative unital symmetric $k$-algebra $A$ and a finite-dimensional unital left $A$-module $M$ such that $M$ is nonprojective and $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_A^i(M,M)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }i>0.$$ In particular, Tachikawa’s second conjecture is false.

Let $A,M$ be as in Theorem 1. For every field extension $K/k$, put $A_K=K\otimes_k A$, $M_K=K\otimes_k M$, and $$\Gamma_K=\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_{A_K}(A_K\oplus M_K)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$ Then $\Gamma_K$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra with the following properties, in the category of finite left $\Gamma_K$-modules.* 1. *Every term of the minimal injective resolution of $\Gamma_K$ is projective, but $\mathop{\mathrm{id}}_{\Gamma_K}\Gamma_K=\infty$.* 2. *There is a nonzero simple module $S$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_{\Gamma_K}^i(S,\Gamma_K)=0$ for every $i\geq0$.* 3. *There is a projective-injective Wakamatsu tilting module $W$ which is not tilting.* *Consequently the classical, generalized, and strong Nakayama conjectures, the Auslander–Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture are false for finite-dimensional algebras over $K$.

Let $k$ be the field in Theorem 1, let $K/k$ be any field extension, and let $\Gamma_K$ be the algebra in Corollary 2. For every integer $n\geq1$, there is a finite-dimensional left $\Gamma_K$-module $C_n$ such that $$\mathop{\mathrm{pd}}_{\Gamma_K}C_n=n.$$ Consequently $\Gamma_K$ has infinite little left finitistic dimension and infinite big left finitistic dimension.

Let $P$ be totally acyclic and let $Q$ be an exact complex of projectives. For every integer $a$ there are natural isomorphisms $$\label{h:comparison-formula}
 H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_G^\bullet(P,Q)
 \simeq\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_G(c_aP,c_0Q)
 \simeq H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_G(P,c_0Q).$$ The first isomorphism is induced by cokernels of shifted chain maps and respects composition. For $a>0$ these spaces are $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_G^a(c_0P,c_0Q)$.

A bounded-below complex $P$ of projectives computes derived maps out of it by chain maps modulo homotopy. Every bounded complex of finite modules has such a projective model with finite terms. In particular, two such models of the same derived object are homotopy equivalent.*


*Suppose a derived triangle is given by $$L\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow R\xrightarrow{\partial}L[1].$$ For projective models $P_L,P_R$ and a chain map $b:P_R\to P_L[1]$ representing $\partial$, a model of $V$ is the two-cell complex $$\label{h:two-cell}
 P_{V,j}=P_{L,j}\oplus P_{R,j},\qquad
 d_j^{P_V}=\begin{pmatrix}d_j^{P_L}&b_j\\0&d_j^{P_R}\end{pmatrix}.$$ Its subcomplex and quotient represent $L$ and $R$, and its connecting map is the specified $\partial$.
Over a symmetric algebra, a derived map between bounded derived objects whose stable image is zero factors in the derived category through a perfect complex.
The trivial extension $R\ltimes DR$ is a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra. In particular, its left and right regular modules are injective in the categories of all unital modules.
The table [a:multiplication] defines an associative unital algebra of dimension ten. Its radical is the span of the eight basis vectors other than $e,f$, and $(\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}C)^5=0$.

The dual regular module $DC$ has projective dimension at most two on both sides. More precisely, $$D(eC)\cong Ce,\qquad D(Ce)\cong eC,$$ and there are exact sequences $$\begin{aligned}
0\longrightarrow Cf\xrightarrow{\rho_t}Ce
 \xrightarrow{\rho_{\ell_{-2}}}Ce
 \xrightarrow{e\mapsto j^*}D(fC)\longrightarrow0,
\label{a:left-dual-resolution}\\
0\longrightarrow fC\xrightarrow{\lambda_u}eC
 \xrightarrow{\lambda_{\ell_0}}eC
 \xrightarrow{e\mapsto v^*}D(Cf)\longrightarrow0.
\label{a:right-dual-resolution}
\end{aligned}$$ Consequently $$\mathop{\mathrm{pd}}_B({}_B E)\le4,\qquad
\mathop{\mathrm{pd}}_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}(E_B)\le4,\qquad
\mathop{\mathrm{id}}_B({}_B B)\le4.
\label{a:dimension-bounds}$$

The augmentation $Cf\to s$ extends to a projective resolution $R\to s$ with $$R_0=Cf,\qquad R_i=Ce\ (i\ge1),\qquad
d_1=\rho_u,\qquad d_{i+2}=\rho_{\ell_i}\ (i\ge0).
\label{a:simple-resolution}$$ It satisfies $$H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_C(R,s)=
\begin{cases}k&a=0,\\0&a\ne0,\end{cases}
\qquad
H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_C(R,C)=
\begin{cases}Ds&a=2,\\0&a\ne2,\end{cases}
\label{a:dual-cohomology}$$ where the second identification is an isomorphism of right $C$-modules.

Put $\mathcal J=T\otimes_C R$, where $R$ is the resolution in [a:simple-resolution]. There is a triangle in the derived category of $T$-modules $$s[2]\longrightarrow\mathcal J\longrightarrow s \xrightarrow{\tau}s[3], \label{e:triangle}$$ and the connecting class generates the Yoneda algebra: $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_T^*(s,s)=k[\tau],\qquad |\tau|=3. \label{e:one-polynomial}$$ The complex $\mathcal J$ is bounded below, has finite projective $T$-terms, and has bounded homology.

The module $X$ is nonprojective and $$\mathcal H^{\ge0}=k[\tau_1,\tau_2],\qquad |\tau_1|=|\tau_2|=3.
\label{e:two-polynomial}$$ In every integer degree, the only nonzero groups are $$\mathcal H^{3m}=\mathcal P_m,\qquad
\mathcal H^{-3m-1}=D\mathcal P_m\qquad(m\ge0).
\label{e:profile}$$ Under these identifications, postcomposition by a shifted $\tau_i$ between negative groups is the transpose of multiplication by $\tau_i$ on the polynomial spaces. The maps $\mathcal H^{-1}\to\mathcal H^2$ given by either class are zero.

Put $$p_f=f\otimes f,\qquad \zeta=f^*\otimes f^*\in E p_f.$$ For every $a,b\in E$, $a\zeta b=\chi(a)\chi(b)\zeta$. The map $i_X:X\to Ep_f$, $i_X(1)=\zeta$, is an embedding with image in $(\mathop{\mathrm{rad}}E)p_f=\Omega X$. Regarded as a map $X\to\Omega X$, it is nonzero stably and spans $\mathcal H^{-1}$.

For every $H\in k^\times$ and every $m\ge0$, the action of $U_H(-)$ on the groups in [e:profile] is $$\left.U_H\right|_{\mathcal H^{3m}}=H^{-m}\,1_{\mathcal P_m}, \qquad \left.U_H\right|_{\mathcal H^{-3m-1}}=H^{m+2}\,1_{D\mathcal P_m}. \label{e:twist-weights}$$ In particular, the negative action is the stated scalar on the entire $(m+1)$-dimensional space.

There is a finite $E$-bimodule $Y$, projective separately as a left and as a right $E$-module, such that $$\label{b:W}
 W^a:=\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_E(X,(YX)[a])
 \cong
 \begin{cases}
 k,&a=-3,0,\\
 0,&a\notin\{-3,0\}.
 \end{cases}$$ For every $H\in k^\times$, there is an ordinary bimodule map $g_H:U_H\to Y$ whose evaluation, under $U_HX=X$, represents a nonzero element of $W^0$. The same $Y$ works for all $H$, and all modules and maps are defined over $k$.

The complex $K$ represents $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E$, has finite projective $E^e$-terms and has homology only in degrees $0,\ldots,4$. The bimodule $c_5K$ is projective on both sides. Consequently its stable image $$\mathcal I=\langle K\rangle=(c_5K)[5]$$ has finite side-projective representatives, as does $\mathcal I[-1]$. One such representative $Y$ of $\mathcal I[-1]$ is obtained by taking four successive finite bimodule cosyzygies of $c_5K$.
The bimodule $Y$ of Lemma 20 satisfies [b:W].

If a bimodule map $v:B\to DB$ factors in the derived category through a perfect $B^e$-complex, then it factors by ordinary bimodule maps through an object of $\mathop{\mathrm{add}}(DB\otimes B)$, where the tensor product has its outer bimodule actions.

For every finite side-projective bimodule $L$, ordinary tensor–Hom adjunction induces a natural isomorphism $$\underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_{E^e}(L,S)\ \cong\ \underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}}_E(LX,X).$$ This assertion does not require $S$ to be side-projective.
For every $H\in k^\times$, there is a stable bimodule map $U_H[1]\to\mathcal I$ with nonzero evaluated stable map $X[1]\to\mathcal IX$.
The map $\Delta^0$ is surjective. For every $a>0$ and every $a\leq-3$, $\Delta^a$ is an isomorphism, and $\Delta^{-2}$ is injective.
The complex $P_Z$ is totally acyclic. Its degree-zero cokernel $Z$ is finite-dimensional and nonprojective.
The module and resolution in [t:cone] satisfy $$H^a\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_\Lambda(P_Z,Z)=0 \qquad(a>0\ \text{or}\ a\leq-2).$$

Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over a field and let $N$ be a finite-dimensional nonprojective left $B$-module satisfying $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_B^i(N,N)=0$ for all $i>0$. Put $$G=B\oplus N,\qquad \Gamma=\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_B(G)^{\mathrm{op}},$$ where endomorphisms compose in the ordinary order. Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{domdim}}({}_\Gamma\Gamma)=\infty,
 \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{id}}_\Gamma\Gamma=\infty.$$ In particular, $\Gamma$ is not self-injective.

For every field extension $K/k$, let $\Gamma_K$ be the algebra in Corollary 2. There is a finite-dimensional projective almost complete tilting left $\Gamma_K^{\mathrm{op}}$-module $P_K$ with infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposable complements.

For every field extension $K/k$ and every integer $L\geq1$, there is an auxiliary finite-dimensional indecomposable symmetric $K$-algebra $T_L$ admitting an idempotent stratification of length at least $L$ in the sense of Chen, Fang and Xi. In particular, $T_L$ has a nonzero proper stratifying ideal, and $\mathcal D(T_L\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ admits a chain of at least $L$ nontrivial standard recollements through successive corner algebras. Here $\mathrm{Mod}$ denotes all left modules and $\mathcal D$ is the unbounded derived category.

purpose: A counterexample to Tachikawa's second conjecture

coverage.checked_domain: The fixed table over F_2[q], embedded in the stated function field: all basis triples and all products with the proposed identity.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exact polynomial arithmetic checks every basis triple and both unit equations. The displayed basis has dimension ten.

coverage.checked_domain: The span of the eight non-idempotent basis vectors: both ideal actions, every radical word product through the fifth power, and the quotient multiplication.
coverage.oracle_basis: A nilpotent two-sided ideal with quotient the product of the surviving field copies is the Jacobson radical. Every spanning word product is checked exactly.
